children: Amid concerns Chinese artificial intelligence developers are misusing or even stealing intellectual property from their U.S. counterparts, Anthropic
called out three Chinese firms for doing so.
Anthropic said it has identified campaigns that targeted some of Claude's “most valuable capabilities,” including agentic capabilities and tool use, coding and data analysis, and logical reasoning.

The AI lab also noted that distillation, which is a training method where less capable models are improved by utilizing outputs from stronger models, was able to deliver a “significant uplift” in their respective domains.

“Additionally, these findings raise concerns about the misuse of user data by [People's Republic of China] AI labs,” Anthropic wrote on its website. “DeepSeek, Xiaomi, and Moonshot fed conversations between their own models and users into Claude. These labs then used Claude’s responses as training data with which to distill Claude’s capabilities. Some of these exchanges included sensitive information, including from individual users, major multinational companies, and state-affiliated actors. Many of these exchanges were relayed from users of third-party model routing services commonly used by users in the United States and Europe. Those sessions contained names, email addresses, company data, and other sensitive data of hundreds of end users in at least a dozen languages. These practices are likely inconsistent with privacy laws and the labs’ own terms of service.”
), Xiaomi, and Moonshot did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Seeking Alpha.
US intelligence agencies, including the FBI,

a statement this week to American AI labs to safeguard their IP after accusing major Chinese AI firms, including DeepSeek and Moonshot AI, of systematically harvesting proprietary data from American models.
This is not the first time that U.S. AI labs have accused Chinese AI labs of using distillation, a practice that has brought ire from U.S. politicians.
Anthropic issued a letter to White House officials and U.S. Senators in June claiming that Alibaba
had used distillation to improve the performance of its models. Anthropic
it had evidence showing that operators linked to Alibaba's Qwen AI lab conducted 28.8M exchanges with Claude through about 25,000 fraudulent accounts.

U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in July that the Trump Administration would be entitled to sanction open-weight models from China if evidence of distillation from American models is verified.

“We are finding watermarks of our U.S. large language models on many of the Chinese models, and that's unacceptable,” Bessent said at the time. “We're going to be looking at that in the coming days or weeks.”
Moonshot AI, which is backed by Alibaba, released Kimi K3 in July, which it said is the world's largest open-weight AI model. Alibaba released a preview of its flagship Qwen 3.8 Max in July.

U.S. and Chinese officials are planning to hold meetings on AI in September. The AI talks, a significant outcome of ‌the U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping's meeting in May, will likely take place before Xi's planned Sept. 24 visit to the U.S.
